name: beautiful-electron
description: Write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Electron desktop applications on Electron 45 + TypeScript: three skills distilled from the Electron security documentation, the Electron process-model and packaging guides, and the facta desktop handbook, plus a drop-in eslint config.

interface.longDescription:
Three skills for Electron desktop developers, distilled from the Electron security documentation, the Electron process-model and packaging guides, and the facta desktop handbook.

electron-best-practices guides new Electron code: the three-process model, the typed preload bridge, the origin- and window-checked IPC policy, a window-free domain and application core, MVVM over the renderer, typed storage with migrations, OS-keystore secrets, fuses and a strict CSP, signed updates, and the unbreakable layer contract.

electron-review reviews a main process, preload bridge, renderer, IPC contract, packaging config, or diff and returns a prioritized report. Architecture and trust zones rank above everything. Every finding cites a file and line, the rule it breaks, and the smallest fix.

electron-port ports a legacy Electron app, a web, Tauri or Qt app, or a generic desktop app to Electron 45 with the same behavior. It ports the original tests first and writes a PORTING.md that lists every deliberate difference.

The skills contain instructions and reference text only. They make no network calls and collect no data. When a Node.js toolchain is available, the skills run tsc, eslint, and vitest on your project; without one, they work from the code alone. A drop-in eslint config is available in the GitHub repository.
capabilities: Review Electron code with cited rules
Port legacy or web desktop apps to Electron
defaultPrompt: Review this Electron preload bridge and list what to fix first
Port this Electron 20 app to Electron 45 with the same behavior
Write an origin-checked IPC handler for this feature

publication.release_notes: Initial release: three Electron skills, the three-process trust contract, and a proven eslint config.
